A.why: Gold spiked crown is a strong, instantly readable silhouette; black and gold reads regal and apart from every reference.
A.fix: Magma cracks are hairline and front-only; add a wide glowing seam visible from above and darken the crown body so it is not a solid gold block.

B.why: Sternum core gem is a good light place but only reads from the front; from above it is a dark box close to blackened iron.
B.fix: Give it one silhouette idea (helm crest or ridged pauldrons) and move glow to where the top camera sees it.

C.why: Horned helm with glowing eyes and a chest gem with a diagonal crack, restrained gold; good face but horns are stubs from above.
C.fix: Lengthen and sweep the horns so the head reads at ARPG distance; carry a seam over the shoulders.

D.why: Gold-rimmed helm with a molten square on top is the best read from the ARPG camera and a natural home for the aura; chest crack fits the brief.
D.fix: Make the grey chest panel basalt black (it drifts toward iron) and add molten seams on back and pauldron tops.

E.why: Generic dark plate with teal accents off-palette; no silhouette idea and glow too small to notice.
E.fix: Remove teal, pick one silhouette idea, consolidate cracks into one bold glowing seam.

F.why: Large saturated blue panels dominate and break the palette; without them the silhouette is generic.
F.fix: Replace all blue with black or molten red, then build up a helm crest or pauldron line.

notes: D and A are close: D has the best top-down light place, A the strongest outline (crown). A merge of A's crown outline with D's molten top gem would be the ideal. All sets leave green trousers visible at the thigh (no leg slot), and all keep magma cracks too thin to read from the ARPG camera.
